checks.description: A fresh harvester is left on the engine's own (shroud-blind) search before the home survey is flown. In all 14 recorded 16:9 openings the first harvester was ordered at 51s to a 4-cell patch 16-17 cells out, so the best field this side could see was past EngineFirstCells (8) for at least the first review of that harvester. If this id is absent: TiberiumSurvey.IsFlown read true too early, the harvester read idle or not-live at spawn, or the yard could already see a field within 8 cells of the first refinery (then there was nothing to fix).

Deferral ends once the harvester's own ground is known within 8 cells or the survey is flown. Three pre-survey harvesters reviewed about every 15s over roughly 51-273s is at most ~35 deferrals; more than 80 means the survey never completed or a harvester kept deferring on ground past the threshold for the whole match.

Earned at 120s was exactly 700 (one load) in all 13 scored 16:9 runs, because the first harvester commuted 16-17 cells. On the engine's search it works ground about 6 cells from its dock and should be unloading a second load before 120s.
Earned at 180s: 2,660 here, median 2,765 over 13 scored runs, only one run ever above 3,300 (3,485). The opponent's median was 4,200.
Earned at 300s: 8,400 here against the opponent's 14,500; median 9,225 over 13 scored runs (opponent median 11,990).

Own harvesters lived 634s on average on home ground (194.8s the round before). Deferring the opening to the engine keeps them within its 15-cell refinery search, so it must not feed the early fleet to raids.
Lifetime income was 42.2 c/s (prior median 38.3). The change only touches the pre-survey opening, so the whole-match rate should not fall.
